elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to an affiliate.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits Company to assign the Agreement without consent to an affiliate.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a merger.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in a merger.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in an acquisition.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in an acquisition.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of its assets.
elements.evidence: The proviso expressly permits assignment without consent to a successor in a sale of substantially all of Company's assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign the Agreement without Customer's prior consent.
elements.evidence: The opening sentence requires the other party's express, prior written consent, and no Vendor assignment exception is added.

elements.element: Customer's consent to a Vendor assignment may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The consent requirement expressly states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor may never assign the Agreement to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: There is no competitor prohibition; Customer could consent to an assignment to a competitor.

elements.element: Vendor has no termination right upon Customer's change of control.
elements.evidence: The operative clause grants no termination right arising from Company's change of control.

elements.element: Customer may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Company may assign without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Customer must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: The successor carve-out contains no written-notice requirement.

elements.element: Vendor may assign the Agreement to a successor without consent.
elements.evidence: Vendor has no successor carve-out and remains subject to the other party's prior written consent.

elements.element: Vendor must provide written notice of an assignment to a successor.
elements.evidence: No written-notice mechanism for Vendor successor assignments is included; such assignments instead require consent.

elements.element: Customer's assignments other than successor assignments require Vendor's consent.
elements.evidence: Company may also assign to an affiliate without consent, even when that affiliate is not a successor.

elements.element: Vendor's consent to Customer's assignments requiring consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: For assignments subject to consent, the clause states that consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

elements.element: Vendor's assignments other than successor assignments require Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: All Vendor assignments remain subject to the other party's express, prior written consent.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor's assignments requiring consent may not be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The clause states that the required consent will not be unreasonably withheld.

result.reason: The redline implements the Customer affiliate and transactional-successor carve-outs and retains a reasonableness-qualified consent requirement for Vendor assignments. It does not prohibit Vendor assignment to a Customer competitor, so the preferred position is incomplete. It also does not provide a mutual successor-assignment right on written notice and exempts Customer affiliate assignments from consent, so the fallback is incomplete. The operative language is internally coherent and preserves the original restrictions on transfer and subcontracting, but it does not reach either complete playbook level.
